title: 1099. Which Indian state shares its border with the maximum number of countries?
hint: Its capital is Gangtok.
summary: Sikkim shares borders with China, Nepal and Bhutan.

title: 1100. Which Indian state has the highest population density?
hint: Its capital is Patna.
summary: Bihar has the highest population density among Indian states.

title: 1066. Which state is the largest producer of rubber in India?
hint: It is located on the southwest coast.
summary: Kerala is India's largest producer of natural rubber.

title: 1082. Which Indian state is known as the 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'?
hint: It shares a border with Bhutan.
summary: Sikkim is associated with the Land of the Thunder Dragon due to its proximity to Bhutan.

title: 1083. Which Indian state has the highest number of national parks?
hint: Its capital is Bhopal.
summary: Madhya Pradesh has the highest number of national parks in India.

title: 1084. Which Indian state is the largest producer of bananas?
hint: Its capital is Chennai.
summary: Tamil Nadu is India's leading producer of bananas.

title: 1085. Which Indian state has the longest national highway network?
hint: It is the largest state by area.
summary: Rajasthan has the longest national highway network in India.

title: 336. Which UNESCO World Heritage Site extends across six Indian states?
hint: It is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots.
summary: The Western Ghats stretch from Gujarat to Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

title: 337. Great Himalayan National Park is located in which state?
hint: Shimla is the capital of this state.
summary: Great Himalayan National Park became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.

title: Which temple is located at Halebidu and is associated with Hoysala architecture?
description: Identify the famous Hoysala temple at Halebidu.
hint: It is dedicated to Shiva.
summary: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu is a major example of Hoysala architecture.

title: What is a gopuram?
description: Identify the architectural element known as a gopuram.
hint: It is usually associated with the entrance of South Indian temple complexes.
summary: A gopuram is a monumental gateway tower, especially prominent in South Indian temples.

title: Which temple is famous for its large gopurams and Dravidian architecture?
description: Identify the major temple complex in Madurai known for its monumental gateways.
hint: It is dedicated primarily to Meenakshi and Sundareswarar.
summary: The Meenakshi Amman Temple at Madurai is famous for its large gopurams and Dravidian architecture.

title: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was commissioned by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
description: Identify the ruler traditionally credited with commissioning the Kailasa Temple at Ellora.
hint: He was a prominent Rashtrakuta king.
summary: Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I is traditionally credited with commissioning the Kailasa Temple at Ellora.

title: How many types of writs are mentioned in the Constitution of India?
description: The Constitution empowers higher courts to issue specific writs for protection of legal and fundamental rights.
hint: The number is five.
summary: The five constitutional writs are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

title: Which writ literally means 'produce the body'?
description: This writ is primarily used to secure the release of a person from unlawful detention.
hint: Its Latin meaning refers to producing the body.
summary: Habeas Corpus literally means 'you may have the body' and is used against unlawful detention.

title: Which writ is primarily used to secure release from unlawful detention?
description: The writ protects personal liberty by requiring justification for detention.
hint: Think of the writ associated with unlawful custody.
summary: Habeas Corpus is primarily used to challenge unlawful detention and secure release where the detention is illegal.

title: Which Roman work mentions Muziris?
description: Which ancient Greco-Roman geographical work provides information about ports such as Muziris?
hint: It was a first-century work describing navigation and trade routes.
summary: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea mentions Muziris.

title: What was Korkai famous for?
description: What economic activity was Korkai especially famous for during the Sangam period?
hint: The Gulf of Mannar was famous for this marine resource.
summary: Korkai was famous for pearl fishing and the pearl trade.

title: 828. Which river is the second longest peninsular river of India?
hint: It flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
summary: The Krishna River is the second longest peninsular river.

title: What is the capital of Tamil Nadu?
description: Identify the capital city of the state of Tamil Nadu.
hint: It is a major city on the Coromandel Coast.
summary: Chennai is the capital of Tamil Nadu.

title: Which city is popularly known as the Manchester of South India?
description: Identify the Tamil Nadu city associated with textile industries and this nickname.
hint: It is an important textile center in western Tamil Nadu.
summary: Coimbatore is popularly known as the Manchester of South India.

title: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within Tamil Nadu?
description: Identify the important river that flows entirely within Tamil Nadu.
hint: It rises in the Western Ghats and reaches the Bay of Bengal.
summary: The Thamirabarani is the longest river flowing entirely within Tamil Nadu.

title: Who built the Krishna Temple at Hampi?
description: The Krishna Temple at Hampi was built by which Vijayanagara ruler?
hint: The temple commemorated a military victory in eastern Andhra.
summary: Krishnadevaraya built the Krishna Temple at Hampi.

title: Which temple at Hampi is known for Ramayana panels?
description: Which Vijayanagara temple is particularly noted for extensive Ramayana-related carvings?
hint: Its name refers to a large number of depictions.
summary: The Hazara Rama Temple is known for its Ramayana panels.

title: 486. Which Buddhist sect spread widely in Sri Lanka?
hint: It is closely associated with Pali literature.
summary: Theravada Buddhism became dominant in Sri Lanka.

title: 487. Who was Ashoka's son that helped spread Buddhism to Sri Lanka?
hint: His sister Sanghamitta also accompanied the mission.
summary: Mahinda played a major role in spreading Buddhism to Sri Lanka.

title: 37. What is the main cause of tides?
summary: Tides are primarily caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon.

title: 38. Which biome is characterized by permafrost?
summary: The tundra biome contains permanently frozen subsoil called permafrost.

title: 1023. Chapchar Kut festival is celebrated in which state?
hint: It belongs to Northeast India.
summary: Chapchar Kut is celebrated in Mizoram.

title: 1024. Vasant Panchami is associated with the worship of which deity?
hint: The deity represents knowledge and learning.
summary: Vasant Panchami is associated with Goddess Saraswati.

title: 1437. Which railway PSU is mainly responsible for executing railway projects in India and abroad?
hint: Its name begins with 'Indian Railway Construction'.
summary: IRCON International executes railway and infrastructure projects in India and overseas.

title: 1438. Which city is the headquarters of the North Central Railway zone?
hint: It is also known as Prayagraj.
summary: North Central Railway is headquartered at Prayagraj.

title: 1439. Which organization owns and operates the Dedicated Freight Corridors in India?
hint: It is a PSU under the Ministry of Railways.
summary: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) develops and operates freight corridors.

title: 1399. Which channel separates Kavaratti and Agatti islands in Lakshadweep?
hint: It is named after the degree of latitude.
summary: The Nine Degree Channel separates Kavaratti from Kalpeni and the islands north of it.

title: 1400. Which factor makes Lakshadweep vulnerable to climate change?
hint: The islands are very low-lying.
summary: Low elevation and sea-level rise pose major risks to Lakshadweep.

title: 1238. Jalori Pass is situated in which state?
hint: Its capital is Shimla.
summary: Jalori Pass is located in Himachal Pradesh.

title: 1239. Which pass connects the Chamba and Pangi valleys?
hint: It is one of the most difficult roads in Himachal Pradesh.
summary: Sach Pass connects Chamba and Pangi valleys.

title: 664. Which is the longest continental mountain range in the world?
hint: It stretches along the western coast of South America.
summary: The Andes are the world's longest continental mountain range.

title: 665. The Andes Mountains extend through how many countries?
hint: Count from Venezuela to Chile.
summary: The Andes pass through seven South American countries.

title: 170. Which National Park became famous due to the reintroduction of cheetahs in India?
hint: Located in Madhya Pradesh.
summary: Kuno National Park became the site of India's cheetah reintroduction project.

title: 171. Which National Park is located in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in Karnataka?
hint: It shares boundaries with Mudumalai and Wayanad.
summary: Bandipur National Park is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

title: 172. Nagarhole National Park is located in which state?
hint: Its capital city is Bengaluru.
summary: Nagarhole National Park is located in Karnataka.

title: 1469. Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
hint: He was killed by Pushyamitra Shunga.
summary: Brihadratha was the last Mauryan ruler and was killed by his general Pushyamitra Shunga around 185 BCE.

title: 1470. Which dynasty succeeded the Mauryan dynasty in Magadha?
hint: Its founder was Pushyamitra.
summary: The Shunga dynasty succeeded the Mauryan dynasty in Magadha after Pushyamitra Shunga overthrew Brihadratha.

title: 1471. Which ancient Greek work provides information about the Mauryan Empire?
hint: It was written by a Greek ambassador who visited Chandragupta Maurya's court.
summary: Indica, written by Megasthenes, provides valuable information about Mauryan India.

title: Who led the Mughal campaign against Shivaji in 1665?
description: Which Mughal general negotiated the Treaty of Purandar with Shivaji?
hint: He was a Rajput ruler from Amber.
summary: Raja Jai Singh I led the Mughal campaign against Shivaji in 1665.

title: What was the Treaty of Purandar signed in?
description: In which year was the Treaty of Purandar signed between Shivaji and the Mughals?
hint: It followed Jai Singh's campaign against Shivaji.
summary: The Treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665.

title: Where was Shivaji detained by Aurangzeb?
description: In which city was Shivaji placed under detention after visiting Aurangzeb's court?
hint: The city was the Mughal imperial capital at the time.
summary: Shivaji was detained at Agra in 1666.
